            <div>
                <h3>The double copy and perturbative teleparallel gravity</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Georg Stettinger</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-11-24</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: hep-th</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>In this paper we analyze the double copy between gluon and graviton amplitudes within the context of teleparallel gravity. We first set up an effective Lagrangian based on minimal assumptions which reproduces the on-shell amplitudes stemming from the double-copy procedure. By straightforwardly computing the three- and four-point amplitude, this double-copy Lagrangian can be constrained up to a few real parameters when expanding to quartic order. For a specific choice of parameters, we find an exact equivalence with perturbative teleparallel gravity. This suggests that the teleparallel formulation might be well suited to make the double copy more transparent from a Lagrangian viewpoint.</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.33146v1" target="_blank">View on arXiv</a>
                    <a href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2611.33146v1" target="_blank">PDF</a>
                </div>
                <hr>
            </div>
            
            <div>
                <h3>Scalar perturbations in extremal Reissner-Nordström geometry: new methods at work</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Giorgio Di Russo, Davide Fioravanti, Francesco Olivi, Marco Rossi</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-11-24</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: hep-th</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>We study scalar radiation emitted by a particle moving along a circular orbit around a four-dimensional extremal Reissner-Nordström black hole. In particular, we calculate the energy fluxes carried by scalar waves to infinity and across the event horizon, as well as the scalar self-force acting on the particle, and express all these quantities as post-Newtonian expansions. Our results for the energy fluxes are in agreement with previous numerical findings in the literature. To solve the radial wave equation, we employ and test two distinct analytic approaches: the first is the so-called \textit{kink method}, a novel alternative stemming from quantum integrability and the second is the Mano-Suzuki-Takasugi method. The perfect agreement of the results highlights the potential of the kink method as a complementary tool for studying wave propagation in black-hole spacetimes.</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.33123v1" target="_blank">View on arXiv</a>
                    <a href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2611.33123v1" target="_blank">PDF</a>
                </div>
                <hr>
            </div>
            
            <div>
                <h3>DEC Fill-ins, the Bartnik--Bray inner mass, and positive mass theorems with untrapped boundary</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Ahmed Ellithy, Vishnu Kakkat, Stephen McCormick</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-11-24</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: math.DG</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>Given a closed $(n-1)$-dimensional manifold equipped with prescribed spacetime Bartnik data, we ask when this can be realised as the boundary of a compact $n$-dimensional initial data set satisfying the dominant energy condition (DEC). This is a natural generalisation of the problem of non-negative scalar curvature fill-ins, where the boundary metric and mean curvature are prescribed. We give conditions on the Bartnik data that suffice to prove the existence of such DEC fill-ins with inner MOTS boundary, and give some applications of these fill-ins.   Our first application of these is a lower bound on the Bartnik--Bray inner mass, which we slightly reformulate here to be a genuine spacetime definition. Our other applications include proving a positive mass theorem for spin initial data with boundary that need not be trapped, and a spacetime Penrose-like inequality that gives a positive lower bound on the mass of an initial data set with boundary in terms of its boundary Bartnik data assuming the spacetime Penrose inequality holds.</p>
                </div>

                    <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.33076v1" target="_blank">View on arXiv</a>
                    <a href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2611.33076v1" target="_blank">PDF</a>
                </div>

            <div>
                <h3>General-relativistic Vlasov disks in external magnetic fields around Kerr black holes</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Paweł Doruchowski, Tomasz Grewenda, David Kofroň, Patryk Mach</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-11-24</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>We investigate stationary general-relativistic kinetic models of a collisionless gas around the Kerr black hole immersed in an external magnetic field. The main focus is put on razor-thin disks confined to the equatorial plane, but geometrically thick disks are also briefly mentioned. We consider distribution functions corresponding to constant canonical energy and constant canonical angular momentum of particles within the disk and obtain analytic expressions for the electric current associated with the gas. More general solutions characterized by distribution functions depending on the energy and the angular momentum are obtained assuming the Schwarzschild background metric. In explicit examples, we investigate disks in the Wald magnetosphere, describing an asymptotically uniform magnetic field.</p>
                </div>

                    <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.33053v1" target="_blank">View on arXiv</a>
                    <a href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2611.33053v1" target="_blank">PDF</a>

                <h3>Scalar-tensor interactions selected through their first-order thermodynamic dynamics</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>David S. Pereira</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-11-24</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>We investigate the restrictive capability of first-order thermodynamics on scalar-tensor gravity. Starting from a general action containing nonlinear curvature dependence, an Einstein-tensor-Hessian coupling, and independent quadratic and cubic scalar-Hessian interactions, we derive the complete effective-fluid quantities. Simultaneously imposing Eckart's heat-conduction and shear-viscosity equations, while accounting for cancellations between interactions, substantially reduces the original operator basis and determines the geometric shear viscosity. Retaining the complete heat-conduction law, we establish an integrability condition that constrains the nonlinear Hessian interactions without prescribing the temperature and thermal conductivity. We construct explicit constitutive pairs and derive the associated thermal evolution, revealing contributions beyond the usual acceleration-aligned description. Remarkably, the thermodynamic integrability condition simplifies the scalar-metric kinetic structure such that imposing covariant degeneracy excludes the remaining nonlinear interactions, recovering the established luminal Horndeski subclass. Nonlinear thermodynamically compatible interactions nevertheless survive when degeneracy is restricted to the scalar-unitary gauge. These results establish a connection between thermodynamic integrability and dynamical degeneracy, demonstrating the potential of first-order thermodynamics as an independent and complementary criterion for selecting gravitational interactions.</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.33033v1" target="_blank">View on arXiv</a>
                    <a href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2611.33033v1" target="_blank">PDF</a>
                </div>
                <hr>
            </div>
            
            <div>
                <h3>The Cosmological Constant as a Clock and the Vilenkin Wavefunction as a Resonance</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Stephon Alexander, Marcell Howard</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-11-24</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>We address the problem of time in quantum gravity using a covariant formulation of unimodular gravity. As a result, the cosmological constant is canonically conjugate to a global four-volume variable, which serves as a clock and leads to a time-dependent Wheeler--DeWitt equation. We construct exact, background-independent solutions related to the full Chern--Simons--Kodama state and demonstrate unitary evolution in minisuperspace. The Chern--Simons functional also provides an intrinsic gravitational clock. These solutions reveal that the Vilenkin wavefunction is a gravitational Gamow resonance, in which its non-normalizability follows from the outgoing boundary condition. The tunneling probability into the expanding branch increases with the positive cosmological constant. These results give a dynamical interpretation of the wavefunction of the universe and clarify the role of its boundary conditions.</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.32987v1" target="_blank">View on arXiv</a>
                    <a href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2611.32987v1" target="_blank">PDF</a>
                </div>

            </div>
            
            <div>
                <h3>Geometrothermodynamics characterization of ABG-AdS black hole immersed by string clouds</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Sayed Farooq Ahmed Shah, Safia Taj</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-11-24</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>Regular black holes, whose singular cores are replaced by smooth geometries sourced by nonlinear electrodynamics, provide a natural setting to study how thermodynamic stability is encoded in spacetime geometry. Conventional stability criteria, however, depend on the choice of thermodynamic potential. Here we develop the quasi-homogeneous geometrothermodynamics of the regular Ayón-Beato--García anti-de Sitter (ABG-AdS) black hole surrounded by a cloud of strings, a Legendre-invariant framework in which no potential needs to be preferred. We show that the entropy, electric monopole charge and AdS radius act as extensive variables obeying a generalized quasi-homogeneity condition, and that the equilibrium manifold then carries three families of thermodynamic metrics. We establish an exact correspondence between response-function anomalies and curvature singularities: the first metric's curvature diverges on the zero-temperature extremal boundary, where the heat capacity vanishes, signaling Davies first-order transitions, whereas the second's diverges precisely where the heat capacity does, pinpointing Davies second-order transitions. The Gibbs free energy displays a swallow-tail structure that reveals a first-order small/large black hole transition, whose metastable region is bounded by these divergences of the heat capacity, together with a Hawking--Page-type transition to thermal AdS. The string-cloud density and the electric charge jointly control the horizon structure, the admissible thermal domain and the stability intervals.</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.32907v1" target="_blank">View on arXiv</a>
                    <a href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2611.32907v1" target="_blank">PDF</a>
                </div>

                <h3>Strong hyperbolicity of puncture-gauge formulations of gravitational theories with second order equations of motion</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Shunhui Yao</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-11-24</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>We prove that the modified CCZ4 (mCCZ4) formulation, used in nonlinear puncture-gauge simulations of (d+1)-dimensional Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity and four-derivative scalar-tensor theory in four dimensions, is strongly hyperbolic for both theories at sufficiently weak coupling, provided that the gauge parameters are chosen to satisfy a cone-separation condition. The proof applies to the full principal symbol of the theories, extending previous analyses based on first-order perturbation theory about the Einstein limit. We establish strong hyperbolicity by recasting the mCCZ4 equations into a formally equivalent second-order system whose derivative structure resembles that of the modified harmonic formulation of Kovács and Reall. This allows us to adapt their covariant characteristic analysis and continuity argument, without assuming that individual eigenvalues or eigenvectors depend analytically on the coupling. We also show that standard CCZ4 in general relativity is strongly hyperbolic in puncture gauge away from two defective degeneracies.</p>
                </div>

                <h3>An uncalibrated effective-one-body waveform model for intermediate-mass-ratio black hole binaries</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Angelica Albertini, Vojtěch Witzany</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-11-24</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>Intermediate-mass-ratio binaries, with mass ratios $q=m_1/m_2\sim10^2-10^4$, are among the most challenging sources for waveform modeling. We present an inspiral-merger-ringdown effective-one-body model for nonspinning, quasicircular binaries with $q>10$, with dynamics built only from analytical post-Newtonian results. It reaches $(2,2)$ unfaithfulness of $10^{-4}-10^{-5}$ against numerical-relativity simulations with $q>10$ and subradian dephasing against second-order self-force waveforms over four-year inspirals at $q=10^4-10^5$. An optimized post-adiabatic implementation enables waveform generation up to two orders of magnitude faster than integrating the full equations of motion.</p>
                </div>

                <h3>Toward Solving the Galactic Foreground Problem in Gravitational-Wave Astronomy with Machine Learning</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Bo Liang, Jinwen Deng, Minghui Du, Hanlin Song, Xilong Fan, Peng Xu, Ziren Luo, Lijing Shao</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-11-24</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>Space-borne gravitational-wave detectors will see tens of millions of Galactic binaries. Resolved, they would form a census of the Galaxy's ultracompact binaries unhindered by dust; unresolved, they are the dominant noise up to a few millihertz for massive black-hole binaries, extreme-mass-ratio inspirals and backgrounds from the early Universe. Separating the two requires the number of binaries, which is ill-defined because binaries exist at every amplitude. We make it an observable by defining a source as a binary above a signal-to-noise threshold. Neural flows count the binaries to within one in 99% of 1 microhertz intervals over 0.5-10 mHz, and nested sampling resolves them, even pairs closer than one frequency bin. The data themselves set a limit: a source is resolvable only if its signal pays for its own description, about 20 nats, which biases even ideal trans-dimensional samplers. Like the diffraction limit in imaging, this Bayesian confusion limit is set by the data rather than by the method, and it governs any superposition of weak sources, from radio surveys and pulsar timing arrays to super-resolution microscopy. For future space-borne detectors, the method turns the Galactic foreground into a definite, calibrated count of binaries with an analytic selection function, the basis for global fits and for tests of population models.</p>
                </div>

                    <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.32800v1" target="_blank">View on arXiv</a>
                    <a href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2611.32800v1" target="_blank">PDF</a>
                </div>

                <h3>Multiscale Zoom-in Lattice Simulation for Inflation</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Xinpeng Wang, Angelo Caravano, Leander Thiele, Misao Sasaki</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-11-24</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: astro-ph.CO</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>Lattice simulations are a powerful tool for studying the nonlinear evolution of inflationary fluctuations. The exponential expansion, however, makes it challenging to cover a broad range of scales relevant for the dynamics, limiting how many e-folds a single fixed grid can follow. We develop a three-dimensional zoom-in lattice method to follow inflationary fluctuations over a broad range of scales from the adiabatic subhorizon regime through horizon crossing. Every few e-folds, the grid is refined into one or more subgrids, with small-scale power injected and large-scale fluctuations inherited from previous generations. Each zoom shifts the resolved band while keeping its dynamic range fixed. This extends the duration over which lattice simulations can follow inflationary fluctuations from a few e-folds to tens of e-folds. In a Starobinsky benchmark evolved for 50 e-folds, the curvature power spectrum agrees with linear theory. In a model with an oscillatory feature, the zoom-in simulations recover the peak seen in a high-resolution fixed-grid run and show scale-dependent non-Gaussianity.</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.32753v1" target="_blank">View on arXiv</a>
                    <a href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2611.32753v1" target="_blank">PDF</a>
                </div>

            </div>
            
            <div>
                <h3>A Gauge Pathway to an Ultralight Axion through a Hidden Portal</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Claudio Corianø`</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-11-24</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: hep-ph</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>We study a gauge realization of an ultralight axion with a hidden $SU(2)$ interaction, an Abelian vector portal, a charged Higgs and a Stückelberg field. The vector absorbs one scalar combination and leaves a physical phase. Its normalization is fixed by the Higgs and Stückelberg scales, while hidden confinement generates its mass. Keeping this phase ultralight requires an additional symmetry: the displayed gauge charges alone allow large phase-dependent scalar interactions. We quantify the suppression required of these interactions. Pure-$SU(2)$ lattice results relate the susceptibility to physical confinement scales; one- and two-loop running illustrate the dependence on the chosen high-energy coupling. We derive the coherent radiation-era density and exhibit an initial angle giving the reference dark-matter abundance for $F_χ\simeq10^{17}\,\GeV$ and zero-temperature mass $m_{χ,0}=3\times10^{-20}\,\eV$. We follow the confined population through number-changing and number-conserving limits and bound its energy contribution. An illustrative inflaton background satisfies the stated vacuum and isocurvature tests, conditional on control of a large portal correction to its potential. Its cold hidden history requires a hidden-to-visible reheating fraction near $5\times10^{-12}$, whose microscopic origin remains an input. A second, gauge-anomaly-free model gives the same physical phase scale using two charged Higgs singlets. These constructions specify conditional cosmological examples and the additional protection and reheating mechanisms needed to complete them.</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.32729v1" target="_blank">View on arXiv</a>
                    <a href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2611.32729v1" target="_blank">PDF</a>
                </div>

            </div>
            
            <div>
                <h3>Inflation at strong mixing as a connection problem: effective field theory, Stokes phenomenon and the cosmological collider</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Sebastian Garcia-Saenz, Yizhou Lu, Sébastien Renaux-Petel</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-11-24</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: hep-th</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>We study a massive field strongly mixed with the curvature perturbation during inflation, in the regime where the latter is described at low energies by a single-field effective field theory (EFT) with a quadratic dispersion relation. What this EFT captures, and what lies beyond it, are encoded in a connection problem, which relates the solutions that define the vacuum at early times to those that describe observables at late times. We solve it with a general method that does not rely on an exact solution. An expansion in the inverse mixing, keeping both fields, yields the EFT as its leading order, with corrections under systematic control. It selects the vacuum of the EFT, fixes a phase that the EFT cannot determine on its own, and describes the heavy mode at all times. Particle production lies beyond all orders of this asymptotic expansion. We show that it arises from a Stokes phenomenon at the complex branch points of the dispersion relation and that, in a rotating basis of the two fields, it reduces to the familiar production of particles with half the heavy mass. A reflection symmetry of the equations of motion, combined with the canonical commutation relations, then determines all exponentially small effects exactly, and with them the solution of the connection problem, which combines particle production with a conversion between light and heavy quanta. Together with the expansion, these exact results give a compact analytical formula for the cosmological collider signal, whose exponential suppression, half of the usual Boltzmann one, directly reflects the halved mass of the produced particles. The expansion only requires a separation of scales and the adiabaticity of the heavy mode, while the reflection symmetry holds for many systems in de Sitter space. We therefore expect this approach to bring physical understanding and simple formulas well beyond the present case.</p>
                </div>

                    <a href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2611.32612v1" target="_blank">PDF</a>
                </div>

                <h3>Analytic response functions of space-based gravitational-wave detectors to ultralight scalar-field dark matter under multiple types of TDI combinations</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Wenqiu Tang, Pan-Pan Wang, Yuezhe Chen, Rui Luo, Cheng-Gang Shao</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-11-24</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>Ultralight scalar fields are important candidates for dark matter. As coherently oscillating fields, they can leave characteristic signatures in space-based gravitational-wave detectors through their coupling to test masses. In this paper, we derive analytic expressions for the response functions of space-based gravitational-wave detectors to ultralight scalar-field dark matter under multiple types of time-delay interferometry (TDI) combinations. Starting from the coupling action between the scalar field and a test mass, we obtain the additional displacement of the test mass and the single-link Doppler response. We then give the general analytic form of the response function for an arbitrary TDI combination and compare the analytic and Monte Carlo numerical results for the optimal combinations A, E, and T. Finally, we analyze the responses of multiple types of TDI combinations, classify them into ordinary and ζ types according to their low-frequency behavior, and give the low-frequency response expressions of the individual combinations. The results can be used to evaluate the sensitivity of space-based gravitational-wave missions such as LISA, Taiji, and TianQin to the mass and coupling parameters of ultralight scalar-field dark matter.</p>
                </div>

                <h3>Area-minimizing surfaces and the rigidity of three-dimensional electrostatic systems</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Rafael Rocha de Farias</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-11-24</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: math.DG</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>We study three-dimensional electrostatic systems, the Riemannian data of static solutions of the Einstein--Maxwell equations with cosmological constant $Λ$, by means of locally area-minimizing surfaces. Such a surface with non-empty boundary on the horizons is a totally geodesic hemisphere and forces the de Sitter system. A closed one in the interior forces a system of product type, one of eight models if the scalar curvature is somewhere positive on it, among them the Bertotti--Robinson, Nariai and cold and ultracold black hole systems. No compactness, asymptotic or pinching assumption is needed. In particular, closed systems without horizons are flat or compact quotients of the Nariai--Bertotti--Robinson system. For compact systems with connected horizon, the electric field vanishes even when the system is not simply connected, and the area of the horizon is either $12π/Λ$, for de Sitter, or at most $4π/Λ$. With several horizons, every horizon whose area does not exceed the sum of the others is stable, minimizes area in its homology class and satisfies an area--charge inequality, with equality only for the charged Nariai systems; its charged Hawking mass and charge therefore lie in the parameter region of the Reissner--Nordström--de Sitter black holes. Compact systems with horizons are spherical space forms with balls removed. Noncompact systems with strictly mean-convex ends have one end, and their horizons are stable and $π_1$-injective and satisfy a strict area--charge inequality.</p>
                </div>

                <h3>Horizon dynamical entropies and phase space topology</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Matteo Bruno, Simone Speziale</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-11-24</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>We study phase space topologies induced by infinite-dimensional norms as a means to solve the problem of 'integrability' of Hamiltonian generators corresponding to diffeomorphisms of a null hypersurface, with the specific goal in mind to compare different prescriptions for the dynamical entropy of black holes, which replaces the area in non-stationary regimes. We first show that for a scalar field, there exists a family of norms that would provide integrability for different polarizations. We then show that a single member of this family applies to the gravitational field, and it is given by the Sobolev norm already considered in the literature. The obstruction to the other candidates lies in the semi-positivity of the metric.</p>
                </div>

                <h3>Entanglement island and Page curve for one-sided rotating Kerr black holes</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Soumen Pari</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-11-24</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: hep-th</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>We investigate the information paradox for one-sided asymptotically flat rotating Kerr black holes formed through gravitational collapse using the island prescription. Near the horizon, the dynamics of a scalar field can be described by an effective two-dimensional theory, which provides the framework for our analysis. We study how rotation affects the location of the island boundary $\partial I$, the Page time, and the scrambling time, treating non-extremal and extremal Kerr black holes separately. For non-extremal black holes, the emergence of an island prevents the unbounded growth of Hawking radiation entropy at late times and restores the unitary Page curve. We further find that the island boundary depends on the location of the cutoff surface, in contrast to the behaviour found for eternal Kerr black holes. In the extremal case, the late-time entanglement entropy of Hawking radiation approaches the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy of the extremal black hole. Our results demonstrate the important role of black hole geometry in determining the behaviour of entanglement entropy and suggest that the island prescription provides a semiclassical resolution of the information paradox for one-sided rotating Kerr black holes.</p>
                </div>

            <div>
                <h3>Exact Mass Multipoles of Distorted Schwarzschild Spacetimes</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Brennen Black</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-11-24</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>Using the isolated-horizon framework, we compute the geometric and mass multipole moments of the Weyl-distorted Schwarzschild horizon without linearizing the distortion. Starting from the exact integral representation we evaluate it in closed form for two cases, a pure quadrupole distortion and a dipole-quadrupole-octupole distortion. For a pure quadrupole we obtain a closed form for all $\ell$ in terms of confluent hypergeometric functions, while for a dipole-quadrupole-octupole distortion we derive a closed-form series solution in the odd-parity coefficient $β$ whose coefficients are exact in the quadrupole coefficient $α_{2}$. We use these results to understand the errors incurred by leading-order approximations. Leading-order approximations in $α_{2}$ misestimate every dimensionless mass multipole by a relative error of roughly $α_{2}$, nearly independent of $\ell$, and for pure linearization most of the error lies in the linearized quadrupole moment rather than the discarded higher multipoles. A simple degree-counting rule determines which orders of distortion contribute to each multipole. As a consequence, the odd-parity component must be small compared with $α_{2}^2$ before it can be neglected. Finally, truncating the series in $β$ at its first $β$-dependent order reproduces the $\ell \leq 6$ multipoles to about $10^{-3}$ for $|β|,|α_{2}| \leq 1/8$.</p>

                <h3>Completing the real-space construction of the canonical harmonic coordinates of Kerr metric</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Zizheng Xing, Xiaokai He, Zhoujian Cao</i></p>

                <div>
                    <p>In this paper, we determine the exact canonical harmonic Kerr metric to all post-Minkowskian (PM) orders within the multipolar post-Minkowskian (MPM) formalism. The metric agrees with the previously constructed 4PM results. Using a formal series ring, we prove that no homogeneous components of Laplacian operator appear in this metric at PM order $n\ge2$. Together with the equality of the linear field with the canonical Kerr solution, this property allows an inductive construction of the canonical MPM metric where all gauge moments vanish. The coordinate transformation linking the canonical harmonic Kerr metric to the Boyer-Lindquist metric is generated by the real part of a complex harmonic radial function. A recent independent construction by Sadu and Vanhove using momentum-space recursion and a residual homogeneous freedom classification yields the same result, providing a cross validation of the closed-form canonical harmonic Kerr metric.</p>

                <h3>Machine learning enables full Bayesian inference for spinning extreme-mass-ratio inspirals</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Bo Liang, Minghui Du, Zhenwei Lyu, Hanlin Song, Jiakai Zhang, Weichen Qin, Chia-Jui Chou, Yi Yang, Jingyi Yu, Ziren Luo, Mingming Sun, Peng Xu, Yue-Liang Wu</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-11-24</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>Extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs), stellar-mass compact objects spiralling into massive black holes, promise to measure the masses and spins of the central black holes, reveal the strong-field environment around them and gauge cosmic distances via millihertz gravitational-wave observations. Yet most forecasts for the parameter inference of these systems assume known source parameters, and broad-prior analyses have addressed only simplified versions of the problem. The joint inversion of all 14 parameters of a spinning source from the complete prior has remained unsolved. Here we solve it for the augmented analytic kludge model: generative networks narrow the complete prior and reveal a ring of degenerate spin directions, and the exact detector likelihood determines the posterior. For a simulated one-year LISA-Taiji observation, within one ring sector we obtain, for the first time, a 14-parameter posterior of a spinning EMRI from the complete prior, the most precise yet obtained for such a source from broad priors. The redshifted mass and spin of the massive black hole are determined to two parts in $10^5$, the mass two orders of magnitude beyond any electromagnetic measurement. The compact object's redshifted mass is measured to one part in $10^4$, and its eccentric, retrograde orbit discriminates between capture channels. The 0.8% distance and sub-square-degree localization are sufficient for dark-siren cosmology. Year-long coherent analysis resolves the inspiral driven by radiation reaction itself.</p>

                <h3>Classical phase space distributions for quantum states in cosmology: General states, operator ordering and the geometry of fading non-commutativity</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Alejandro Corichi</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-11-24</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>In earlier work with Ashtekar and Kesavan we showed that, for linear fields in any FLRW background, the vacuum defines a probability distribution $ρ_o$ on the classical phase space whose moments are exactly the Weyl-ordered $n$-point functions. We extend that analysis in four directions. First, for an arbitrary state $Ψ$ we give an explicit formula, in the Bargmann representation, for the distribution $ρ_Ψ$ that reproduces all Weyl-ordered expectation values. For pure states it is non-negative precisely for coherent and squeezed states, each the Gaussian of a compatible Kähler metric, and the Gaussian smoothing needed to make it positive is either zero or the full coherent-state width. Second, for linear observables every operator ordering differs from the Weyl ordering by explicit products of $c$-number commutators. Third, for two linear observables in a pure Gaussian state, the classical correlation coefficient, the ratio of commutator to anticommutator and the squeezing are functions of a single angle between their Hamiltonian vector fields; this bounds the departure of arbitrarily ordered $n$-point functions from the moments of $ρ$. Fourth, for fields in FLRW the equality holds at arbitrary, possibly different, times and for every homogeneous isotropic quasi-free state. In de Sitter the non-commutative corrections fall as $e^{-N}$ for field and momentum and as $e^{-3N}/3$ for the field at two times. For the state inherited from inflation they stay suppressed in the radiation era, by the inverse occupation number, except near the nodes of the mode functions. The same squeezing entangles the modes $\pm\vec k$ relative to the radiation-era vacuum and makes displaced-parity measurements violate Bell inequalities, so the positive distribution describes a specified family of observables, not all measurements.</p>
                </div>

                <h3>Prospects for Detecting Post-merger Signals from Binary Neutron Stars with Future Gravitational-Wave Detectors</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Jingwang Diao, Teng Zhang, Xingjiang Zhu</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-11-24</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>The post-merger (PM) phase of binary neutron star (BNS) mergers carries information about the merger remnant and the dense-matter equation of state, but its observational prospects remain uncertain. We compare two approaches to accessing this emission: the stochastic gravitational-wave background (SGWB) from the BNS population and direct PM-band detections of individually resolved mergers. Using a unified inspiral--merger--post-merger (IPM) waveform prescription and the same astrophysical population model for both calculations, we evaluate representative third-generation detector configurations involving ET, CE, and a dedicated kilohertz detector. For the representative detector networks considered, the baseline IPM model predicts that the all-source, broadband BNS SGWB exceeds the adopted detection threshold across the local merger-rate interval. In contrast, the kilohertz PM-band SGWB remains below this threshold. For individual events, over $R_0=7.6$--$250~{\rm Gpc}^{-3}\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$, the baseline IPM model predicts approximately $5$--$174$ PM-band candidates per year for the dedicated kilohertz detector, whereas the numerical-relativity cases considered here yield approximately $0.07$--$7~{\rm yr}^{-1}$.</p>

                <h3>Beyond the Thermodynamic-Volume Limit in Holographic Complexity</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Di Wu, Robert B. Mann</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-11-24</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: hep-th</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>In the large black hole regime, holographic complexity obeys a thermodynamic-volume scaling law, while the finite-size approach to this limit remains unresolved. In this Letter, we develop an analytic description of finite-size corrections to this scaling for complexity of formation in the complexity=volume (CV) proposal of odd-dimensional equal-spinning Myers-Perry-AdS black holes. We find that the leading finite-size correction retains state dependence that is absent from the limiting thermodynamic-volume law. This correction changes sign at a distinguished Critical Horizon Ratio (CHR), where the generic leading finite-size contribution vanishes and convergence to the thermodynamic-volume law is correspondingly accelerated. We further determine the dimension dependence of the CHR analytically, showing that it approaches a finite nonextremal value at large dimension with a calculable leading finite-dimensional correction. These results show that the finite-size approach can provide a new probe of holographic structure, motivating its exploration across different realizations of holographic complexity and its eventual characterization in the dual field theory.</p>

                <h3>A cubic theory of gravity with quasitopological-like properties for compactified cosmologies</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Vicente Aguilar, Fabrizio Canfora, Vicente García, Alex Giacomini, Julio Oliva</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-11-24</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: hep-th</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>We identify a cubic combination of curvature invariants in dimension $D=7$ that when added to the Einstein-Hilbert action, yields a healthy cosmological evolution in four dimensions after compactification on a constant-curvature internal space of dimension three. For generic backgrounds it leads to fourth-order field equations, nevertheless, on a warped product of a spatially flat, homogeneous and isotropic four-dimensional universe with a constant-curvature space of radius $b(t)$, the constraint is of first order in the scale factor $a(t)$ and in $b(t)$, while the remaining equations are of second order. Requiring this property uniquely singles out the cubic theory. We study the solutions describing a four-dimensional de Sitter Universe in direct product with an internal space of stabilized radius and evaluate its linear stability under time-dependent perturbations, showing that for a given sign of the curvature of the internal space, stability of the static solution fixes the sign of the higher curvature coupling. We also argue that linearized scalar perturbations depending on the spatial coordinates obey equations with at most two time derivatives. Finally, we numerically evolve the homogeneous and isotropic system non-linearly and present evidence that for a positive bare cosmological term $Λ_0$ and a hyperbolic compact space, the singularity formation present in GR in this ansatz is pushed into the future by increasing the higher-curvature coupling.</p>

                <h3>A source-based decomposition of thermal noise for mechanical system design</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Vermeer Bonhomme, Matthew Evans</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-11-23</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: astro-ph.IM</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>Thermal noise limits the sensitivity of precision mechanical instruments. We present a thermal- noise formulation for lumped-element mechanical systems that writes the total displacement thermal noise at the readout as the sum of contributions from all dissipative elements. For each contribution, we separate the thermal force generated by the element from its transfer to the readout. This decomposition provides simple design rules for comparing contributions from elements in series and in parallel and identifying the dominant noise source. It applies to frequency-dependent dissipation and to elements at different steady temperatures under local thermal equilibrium. We use it to identify the frequency regimes in which parallel and series dissipation dilution reduce displacement thermal noise. We then use examples of a pendulum on a lossy support, a rotational flexure, and rigidly mounted lunar optics to show how support noise can dominate even when the support has little effect on the system dynamics. Finally, a feedback-controlled suspension illustrates how sensing and actuation noise can be included in the same displacement-noise budget.</p>

                <h3>Anisotropic Fluid Inhomogeneous Cosmology</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Mariano Cadoni, Andrea Cozzumbo, Riccardo Murgia, Matteo Pili, Mirko Pitzalis, Andrea P. Sanna, Matteo Schulz, Ilaria Usai</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-11-23</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>We propose a new framework for inhomogeneous cosmology based on General Relativity sourced by an anisotropic fluid. The model is parametrized by a single input function, the radial Misner--Sharp mass distribution at different redshifts, and admits exact solutions to Einstein's equations. Going beyond the standard assumption of small metric perturbations, it provides a fully relativistic framework to describe the non-linear regime of cosmic structure formation. The Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker (FLRW) cosmology is recovered both at early times and -- on large scales only -- at late times. Our Anisotropic Fluid Inhomogeneous Cosmology (AFIC) model provides a natural mechanism through which matter inhomogeneities give rise to late-time acceleration. The extensive term driving this effect does not enter the exact metric solution and therefore does not contribute to the local gravitational potential. Rather, it emerges as a genuinely large-scale effect induced by the inhomogeneous distribution of matter at late times. This mechanism may provide a physical interpretation of the results from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI). Finally, we present a simple analytical realization of the model and use it to provide an estimate of the present-day effective dark energy density.</p>

                <h3>The Relaxation of Quantum Near-Extremal Black Holes. (I) Microcanonical States, Pruning of Quasinormal Modes, and the Aretakis Instability</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Roberto Emparan, Sameer Murthy, Stefano Trezzi</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-11-23</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: hep-th</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>The late-time relaxation of a near-extremal black hole is classically governed by an infinite tower of purely damped quasinormal modes. This poses a puzzle: the higher overtones decay at rates much larger than the energy $E$ of the black hole above extremality, so they would need black hole states below the extremal mass. We resolve it by including the quantum fluctuations that become large when $E$ falls below a scale $E_b$. We compute the retarded Green's function of a probe of conformal dimension $Δ$ in a black hole of fixed energy, and find that each classical mode splits into a pair of poles with real parts set by $E_b$. The perturbed black hole decays as an unstable quantum system, and a pair is a resonance, i.e., a quasinormal mode, only if its energy lies within the accessible black hole spectrum. This prunes the tower to finitely many modes, all damped faster than $Δ^2E_b$, and below $E=Δ^2E_b/2$ none is left. For generic $Δ$, the response of the black hole decays first as $t^{-2Δ}$ and finally as $t^{-3/2}$, with an exponential stage in between if $E\ggΔ^2E_b$.   The same quantum effects bear on the Aretakis instability of extremal black holes, in which transverse derivatives of a perturbation grow without bound on the horizon. Like the tower of modes, it originates in the scale invariance of the classical throat, which the quantum fluctuations break. The $t^{-2Δ}$ decay, which is the boundary counterpart of the Aretakis growth, ends by $t\sim1/E_b$, when the throat ceases to be classical, and by then horizon derivatives have grown only to a finite value. Their unbounded growth is an artifact of taking the semiclassical limit before the late-time one, two limits that in quantum mechanics do not commute.</p>

                    <p>Coupling a shift-symmetric scalar field to the Gauss-Bonnet invariant modifies black holes (BHs) via scalar hair. Here we consider this field to be the Goldstone of a complex scalar field with a symmetry-breaking potential. For BHs of a size comparable with the inverse mass gap, the gapped field tries to restore the symmetry close to the horizon, enhancing the departure from standard BHs.                 <h3>Quantum black hole evaporation from thin shell collapse: a complete effective picture</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Michał Bobula, Francesco Fazzini</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-11-23</b></p>

            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>Quantum gravity is expected to play a central role in resolving classical singularities and providing a complete, predictive spacetime picture. In this paper, we develop an effective model inspired by loop quantum gravity that aims to fulfill this expectation, providing a unified description of thin shell collapse, black hole formation, evaporation, and remnant dynamics. The framework exhibits general validity, holding across different effective equations of motion, matter sources, and evaporation laws. Specifically, we incorporate backreaction within a quasi-static approximation, modeling the radiation as null dust and matching the ingoing and outgoing fluxes across an evaporation surface using the Darmois-Israel junction conditions. For an evaporation law governed by the Stefan-Boltzmann law, we find that the final stage of evaporation yields an extremal black hole extending into a new asymptotic region, featuring both event and Cauchy horizons. Conversely, under the Schwinger approach, no event or Cauchy horizons form, instead, a temporary dynamical trapped region emerges, and the resulting spacetime remains globally hyperbolic. Under this variant, our model predicts a horizonless null remnant escaping to future null infinity.</p>

                <h3>Refined Rényi Entropy from Replica-Geometry Tensor Networks</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Qiang Wen, Haocheng Zhong, Yiwei Zhong</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-11-23</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: hep-th</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>Holographic tensor networks are a central route to understanding the mechanism behind the holographic duality, but standard fixed-graph constructions with maximally entangled links face a structural obstacle. Their leading entanglement spectra are flat, so their Rényi entropies do not depend on the replica index. This is in sharp contrast with holographic conformal field theories, where a tensionful cosmic brane makes the refined Rényi entropy $n$-dependent. Capturing this replica dependence is therefore an important test of tensor-network descriptions of holographic entanglement. We construct an explicit family of replica-dependent geodesic graphs that reproduces this behavior while keeping the links maximally entangled. For each replica index $n$, geodesics are emitted from the replicated boundary with the same local, isotropic intersection measure. They perfectly tessellate the selected replica geometry, so the $n$-dependence of their intersection counts comes from the geometry. Tensor-network models on these graphs reproduce the cosmic-brane prescription for refined Rényi entropy by counting crossing threads. Their cross-copy endpoint density also agrees, in CFT$_2$, with a boundary reconstruction within the additive linear combination proposal, providing a check beyond the total entropy. In higher dimensions, we further obtain an analytic large-separation decay law for this density.</p>

                <div>
                    <p><i>Anna Liu, Mick Wright, Jef Heynen, Eungwang Seo, Isaac C. F. Wong, Disha Hegde, Laura E. Uronen, Harsh Narola, Chris Van Den Broeck, Martin Hendry, Tjonnie G. F. Li, Otto A. Hannuksela, Justin Janquart</i></p>

            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>

                <div>
                    <p>Just like light, gravitational waves may be gravitationally lensed by massive objects along their travel path, however, this has not been observed so far. GW231123 is the most massive binary black-hole merger observed to-date, and quasi-circular gravitational wave analyses infer high masses and spin parameters that are particularly sensitive to the waveform model used. Here we investigate whether gravitational lensing can account for these features. We model the signal as a superposition of multiple overlapping images of the same merger and find support for lensing across four waveform models. The lensing interpretation reduces the support for these high spins, bringing both the inferred spins and masses into closer agreement across waveform models. A comparison with a background of unlensed signals gives the lensing interpretation an estimated significance of $3.96^{+0.68}_{-0.30}σ$. This makes lensing a compelling interpretation of this event but is insufficient for a definitive claim.</p>

                <h3>How to Play a Black Hole: Understanding Quasinormal Mode Excitation</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Lucía Vélez-Tartajo, Vitor Cardoso, Jaime Redondo-Yuste</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-11-23</b></p>

            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>

                <div>
                    <p>Understanding the excitation of black hole quasinormal modes is essential for interpreting gravitational-wave signals and inferring black hole properties from them. In this work, we investigate the excitation of the quasinormal modes of Schwarzschild black holes under controlled probes. In the absence of a source, we find that broader initial data suppresses mode excitation, enhancing the relative contribution of the late-time tail, while data localized near the light ring strongly suppresses overtones relative to the fundamental mode. On the other hand, plunging sources give rise to two distinct ringdown stages, associated with scattered radiation generated during the particle's infall and with the particle crossing the light ring. Finally, we investigate how much of the signal is sourced from the strong-field region by switching off the source at some finite radius. The resulting waveform is exponentially close -- in cutoff radius -- to that of a standard infall. These results provide insight into the dependence of QNM excitation on the properties and dynamics of the perturbation, and offer a controlled setting in which to investigate the origin of black hole ringdown.</p>

                <h3>A Kerr-black-hole worldline action to $\mathcal{O}(G^5)$</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Yilber Fabian Bautista, Mathias Driesse, Kays Haddad, Gustav Uhre Jakobsen</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-11-23</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: hep-th</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>We establish a worldline action which correctly reproduces Kerr-black-hole dynamics up to fifth order in Newton's constant in a physical post-Minkowskian counting. This encompasses operators up to second order in the Riemann curvature tensor and up to fourth order in the spin tensor. Doing so entails performing the full effective-field-theory computation of the amplitude for a gravitational-wave scattering off of a spinning compact object up to four-loop order, and matching the result to the predictions from linear black hole perturbation theory. Quadratic-in-curvature operators which must be added to match successfully include time-reversal anti-symmetric ones at linear and cubic spin orders, capturing absorption across the black hole horizon, and conservative quadratic-in-spin ones. As an immediate application of our action, we compute the leading-order change in spin magnitude, and reproduce the leading change in mass, for a Kerr black hole in a scattering event with a second compact body, considering a generic orientation of the black hole's spin.</p>

                <h3>Late-time cosmic acceleration from matter inhomogeneities: constraints from DESI DR2 and SNe Ia</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Mariano Cadoni, Andrea Cozzumbo, Riccardo Murgia, Matteo Pili, Mirko Pitzalis, Andrea P. Sanna, Matteo Schulz, Ilaria Usai</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-11-23</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: astro-ph.CO</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>We present the first observational constraints on the Misner-Sharp (MS) mass of the universe, within a newly proposed exact General Relativity solution providing a non-perturbative description of nonlinear cosmic structure formation. At early times, when statistical homogeneity and isotropy are satisfied, our model reduces to usual FLRW cosmology, accommodating Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) data. At late times, the departure from homogeneity and isotropy on scales $\lesssim 200$ Mpc -- codified in the scale-dependent redshift distribution of the MS mass -- naturally induces cosmic acceleration, through an extensive term generated by the MS mass asymptotic limit on large scales. We derive the MS mass from Baryon Acoustic Oscillation data from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) and Type Ia Supernovae, obtaining a value of the cosmological constant in agreement with $Λ$CDM results. We outline broader implications and future observational prospects, highlighting how multi-probe strategies -- particularly CMB lensing and the late Integrated Sachs-Wolfe effect -- can ultimately test this solution to the dark energy puzzle.</p>

                <h3>The Hidden Simplicity of the Classical Limit</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Yilber Fabian Bautista, Stefano De Angelis, David A. Kosower, Donal O'Connell, Matteo Sergola</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-11-23</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: hep-th</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>We study the classical limit of two-to-two massive-scalar amplitudes at all orders of perturbation theory. We compute these amplitudes in the probe limit for several theories: a family of scalar theories, electrodynamics, and $\mathcal{N}=8$ supergravity with half-BPS matter. We show that related multiple-emission classical amplitudes obey a simple factorization derivable from the usual factorization of quantum amplitudes. The classical factorization, which reflects the second-order nature of classical dynamics, holds in more general theories --- including gravity. We further show that both the multiple-emission and the two-to-two classical amplitudes have a simple organization in terms of weighted trees. This allows a recursive computation to all orders in the probe limit. The probe's trajectory emerges as a generating function of trees. The required boundary conditions are given by the Feynman $i \varepsilon$ prescription, leading to a novel worldline Green's function. In our approach, the rich classical dynamics arises from simple combinatorics.</p>

                <h3>Tidally Induced Coda: Double Transients from Black Hole-Star Binary Encounters with Massive Black Holes</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Konstantinos Kritos, Rosalba Perna</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-11-23</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: astro-ph.HE</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>Dense stellar environments surrounding massive black holes (MBHs) provide a natural setting for dynamical interactions that can produce transient electromagnetic and gravitational-wave sources. In particular, the tidal field of an MBH can strongly perturb binaries undergoing close encounters with it, driving their internal orbits to extreme eccentricities. Here, we investigate the outcomes of such interactions for binaries composed of a stellar-mass black hole (BH) and a star. Using direct few-body scattering experiments with the code SpaceHub, we explore hyperbolic encounters between BH-star binaries and MBHs. We systematically quantify the probabilities of different dynamical outcomes as functions of the binary orbital parameters and MBH mass, with particular emphasis on a channel in which the tidally induced eccentricity triggers a micro-tidal disruption event ($μ$TDE), as the star is disrupted by its BH companion, followed by accretion of the stellar debris onto the MBH. We derive fitting formulae for the $μ$TDE cross section and for the time delay between the two resulting flares, finding that the latter can be a few months for an MBH of $10^6\,M_\odot$. These double transients offer a distinctive observational signature of $μ$TDEs. We estimate event rates ranging from a few to $\sim 100\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$ within a luminosity distance of $40\,{\rm Gpc}$.</p>

                <h3>On the existence of constants of motion for multipolar test-body dynamics</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Paul Ramond</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-11-23</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>We show that the conservative equations of motion of an extended test body, with force and torque sourced by spin-induced and adiabatic tidal multipoles of arbitrary order, are the flow of the Hamiltonian $H=-\tfrac12μ^2+μU$, where $μ$ is the body's kinematic mass and all multipoles enter through a covariant scalar potential $U$. For such bodies, a certain notion of mass and a spin norm are shown to be exactly conserved, at all multipolar orders and in any background. We then apply our framework to the Kerr spacetime, and construct extensions of the Carter and Rüdiger constants through hexadecapolar order (quartic in spin). They are found to exist if, and only if, the body's multipoles are those of a Kerr black hole. Together with the energy and angular momentum, they make the dynamics of a spinning test black hole in Kerr perturbatively integrable through that order. Lastly, at the next, quintic-in-spin order, an analytic criterion implemented numerically reveals that neither constant admits a continuation, for any conservative multipoles. In the conservative, test-body limit, black-hole binaries thus carry a dynamical hidden symmetry shared by no other compact objects, which persists to high multipolar order but ultimately breaks.</p>

                <h3>Optimal Statistic for a Stochastic Gravitational Wave Background using Pulsar-Timing--Astrometry Cross Correlations</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Kimberly K. Boddy, Jeffrey S. Hazboun, Kris Pardo</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-11-23</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>Astrometric measurements have emerged as a viable probe of gravitational waves (GWs), complementing pulsar timing searches by providing overlapping and higher GW frequency coverage. At its core, the search for GWs using astrometry is very similar to the search with pulsar timing data: GWs induce a change in pulse arrival times along the line of sight to a pulsar and a transverse angular deflection in the apparent position of a star. In analogy to pulsar timing, we develop a correlation statistic between pairs of stellar deflections for astrometry to search for a stochastic GW background. With a common formalism for both astrometry and pulsar timing, we also develop the cross-correlation statistic between stellar deflections and pulsar timing residuals. We estimate the signal-to-noise ratios from the correlation statistics and provide scaling laws in the weak- and intermediate-signal regimes.</p>

                <h3>Enhancing eccentricity through tidal resonance in binary neutron star systems</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Ivan Markin, Natalie Williams, Tim Dietrich</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-11-23</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>Orbital eccentricity of binary neutron star systems is a key parameter to reveal their formation history. Since binaries formed in isolation are expected to circularize long before merger, measurable eccentricity suggests dynamical formation in dense stellar environments. However, using numerical-relativity simulations, we show that eccentricity can be introduced in the late inspiral of an initially quasicircular binary, due to the $f$-mode resonance of one of the stars. We simulate the merger of two highly spinning neutron stars, one star spinning prograde and the other retrograde. Persistent tidal resonance with the $f$ mode of the retrograde-spinning star is observed, accompanied by a gradual change of its spin due to angular momentum transfer from the orbit. This spin change can be well explained by a simple resonance locking model that accounts for the spin-dependent shift of the $f$-mode frequency. These findings reveal an origin of eccentricity in binary neutron stars that is independent of their formation history and provide important information for modeling binary neutron star dynamics with rapidly spinning stars.</p>

                <h3>Near-boundary and near-horizon momentum--Krylov response in noncommutative-inspired BTZ spacetime</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>F. A. Brito, F. G. Costa, J. A. V. Campos</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-11-23</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: hep-th</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>We compute the proper radial momentum of a massive probe falling into a Lorentzian-smeared, noncommutative-inspired BTZ black hole at fixed asymptotic mass, and use it as the growth rate of momentum--Krylov complexity. In the BTZ limit the accumulated complexity is $\mathcal{K}_0 = X(\coshτ- 1)$. With smearing, the initial growth coefficient is $F'_α(X)/4$, while the late-time exponent is the surface gravity $F'_α(x_+)/2$. The two depend differently on the smearing parameter, so the deformed response is not a rescaled BTZ curve; we show this analytically and confirm it numerically. For a distant release point the early response approaches BTZ, whereas the late-time rate does not. A BTZ black hole with the same Hawking temperature reproduces the response to within about ten percent, and the remaining difference is set by the early/late mismatch. A Gaussian mass profile gives the same picture. The horizon radius and the surface gravity vanish at the critical smearing with exponents $1/2$ and $3/2$. At fixed mass the boundary stress tensor coincides with that of BTZ, but the $z^3$ Fefferman--Graham coefficient and the lengths of boundary-anchored geodesics do not.</p>

                <h3>Relativistic dynamical friction and accretion for Kerr black holes</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Nicholas Speeney, Soumodeep Mitra, Emanuele Berti, Andrea Maselli, Sumanta Chakraborty</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-11-23</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>Extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) observed by LISA will probe the environments of massive black holes (BHs), including the dark matter (DM) overdensities expected to form around them. We compute the relativistic dynamical friction and accretion experienced by a non-spinning compact object on circular equatorial orbits around a Kerr BH embedded in a collisionless DM distribution, extending previous results in Schwarzschild. The DM is modeled as a spike grown adiabatically from an initial Hernquist profile, and the momentum transfer is obtained by integrating relativistic scattering and capture cross sections over the full, generically anisotropic phase space seen by the secondary. Far from the primary the friction tracks the local DM density, which increases with spin. Near the innermost stable circular orbit of rapidly spinning BHs $(a\gtrsim 0.37)$, however, frame dragging forces bound DM particles to co-rotate, so that the secondary is overtaken by the surrounding medium: the friction weakens and eventually reverses sign where the DM density peaks. We show that a similar reversal can be mimicked around a non-rotating BH if the initial halo carries large net angular momentum, although this requires anisotropies beyond those found in cosmological simulations. We also show that commonly used Chandrasekhar-like prescriptions, which depend only on the local density, can overestimate the friction force. Our results demonstrate that the full phase-space structure of the environment must be included when modeling DM effects on EMRIs.</p>

                <h3>Lyapunov Stability of a Schwarzschild Black Hole Surrounded by the Kiselev Anisotropic Fluid</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Saswati Roy, Paramita Debnath, Shubham Kala, Hemwati Nandan</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-11-23</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>We investigate the geodesic structure and the stability of circular orbits around a Schwarzschild black hole surrounded by a Kiselev anisotropic fluid, characterised by the equation-of-state parameter $ω$ and the normalisation parameter $N$. We consider six representative values, $ω=-1,-2/3,-1/3,0,1/3$ and $1$, over the admissible range of $N$ determined by the horizon structure, including the corresponding extremal limits. Using the effective potentials for null and timelike geodesics, we determine the photon sphere, the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO) and the outermost stable circular orbit (OSCO), and examine their stability through coordinate-time Lyapunov exponents. The photon sphere is unstable for all values of $ω$ and $N$ considered. Its instability weakens with increasing $N$ for $ω\leq0$ and vanishes at extremality for $ω=-1$ and $-2/3$, whereas it varies non-monotonically with $N$ for $ω=1/3$ and strengthens for $ω=1$. For $ω=-1$ and $-2/3$, stable circular orbits are confined between the ISCO and the OSCO, which merge at a critical value of $N$ beyond which no stable circular orbits exist. In contrast, for $ω\geq-1/3$ stable circular orbits exist at all radii beyond the ISCO, whose location varies with $N$. We also derive a closed-form expression for the squared coordinate-time Lyapunov exponent $(λ_t^T)^2$, valid for arbitrary $ω$, whose sign changes exactly at the ISCO and OSCO, so that the Lyapunov criterion reproduces the boundaries of stable circular motion. The Schwarzschild--de Sitter, mass-shifted Schwarzschild and Reissner--Nordström geometries are recovered as special cases, and the results may have implications for black-hole shadows, thin accretion discs and quasi-periodic oscillations.</p>

                <h3>Schwarzschild-de Sitter space is not rigid</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Philippe G. LeFloch, Luc Rozoy</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-11-23</b></p>

            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>Starting from any compact sub-extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter region with positive cosmological constant, we construct a family of static axisymmetric vacuum solutions with two additional black-hole horizons, each of prescribed area. All horizons and the symmetry axis are regular, and the metric and lapse are real analytic up to the boundary. As the mass parameter tends to zero, the metric and lapse converge smoothly to the reference solution away from two antipodal points on its sphere of maximal lapse. Rescaling near either added horizon yields the Schwarzschild spatial metric in the limit. For small prescribed mass, the lapse attains its maximum precisely on one equatorial circle. Its Hessian is negative definite in the transverse plane, with the smaller eigenvalue magnitude asymptotic to a positive constant times the added mass. Nearby regular level sets are tori. The proof combines gluing at separated scales with uniform elliptic estimates. An integral condition removes infinitesimal translations of each Schwarzschild model, while a localized tensor source restores solvability of the linearized equation. Matching the local Schwarzschild corrections to a global Green tensor identifies the leading source coefficients. Reflection makes these coefficients equal, and varying the common radial position of the centers makes them vanish. A radial Green function and the heat equation on the sphere determine the angular variation of the lapse and the geometry of its maximum set.</p>

                <h3>Analytic $k$-essence Inflation</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>V. K. Oikonomou</i></p>

            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>

                <div>
                    <p>In this work we develop a fully analytic $k$-essence inflation solution which is compatible with the observational constraints on inflation, without the need for the slow-roll assumption being imposed dynamically in the field equations. The analytic solution is obtained for a kinetic scalar sector of the form $K(X)= \frac{X^n}{X_s^{n-1}}$ and for the scalar field satisfying a tracking condition $\dotφ^2=γH^{-m}$. For this class of theories, the sound speed of the primordial curvature perturbations is constant, so no gradient instabilities occur in the theory. The Hubble rate, the scale factor and the scalar field can be analytically expressed as functions of the cosmic time, and the observational indices of inflation depend solely on the parameters $n$ and $m$. The resulting evolution is inflationary and it develops a pressure singularity a few $e$-foldings after the end of inflation. However, using qualitative and quantitative numerical arguments, we show that the pressure singularity is classically avoided when the matter fluids of radiation and cold dark matter are taken into account.</p>

                <h3>Fate of Vainshtein Screening for UV/IR Mixing with a $P(X)$ Higgs Classicalizer</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Eléana Berteaux, Florian Nortier</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-11-23</b></p>
                </div>
                <div>
            <p>Categories: hep-ph</p>
                </div>
                <div>
                    <p>Classicalization is a non-Wilsonian framework in which an effective field theory self-completes above its strong-coupling scale by generating semiclassical objects that decay into many soft quanta, thereby realizing ultraviolet-infrared mixing. A key requirement of this mechanism is that the force carrier be lighter than the strong-coupling scale. A natural application would be to embed classicalization in the electroweak Higgs sector to address the little hierarchy problem. In this work, we investigate whether Higgs classicalization can occur within the $P(X)$ class of gauged k-essence and k-chameleon models. For classicalization to occur, the theory must support Vainshtein screening around a sharply localized source. Our results show that it fails to do so, even when one attempts to engineer a symbiosis with chameleon screening through a gauge kinetic function, owing to a strong-coupling breakdown inside the screening region. These $P(X)$ theories therefore fail to provide a suitable framework for Higgs classicalization. Nevertheless, we emphasize that our results, obtained for a specific class of models, should not be interpreted as a no-go theorem for Higgs classicalization.</p>

                    <p>Using worldline effective field theory, we compute the conservative finite-size contributions to the impulse and scattering angle of nonspinning compact binaries in massless scalar-tensor theories with a scalar-Gauss-Bonnet coupling through third post-Minkowskian (3PM) order.                 <h3>Detecting Frame Dragging Effect with Next-Generation Spaceborne Clocks in a LEO-DRO Satellite Configuration</h3>
                <div>
                    <p><i>Li-Fang Li, Hanlin Song, Xing Bian, Tong Liu, Shao-Jiang Wang, Song He, Yang Li, Jiaxing Leng, Ziren Luo, Peng Xu, Rong-Gen Cai</i></p>
                    <p><b>Published: 2026-11-23</b></p>

            <p>Categories: gr-qc</p>

                <div>
                    <p>Our approach employs a satellite constellation comprising one satellite in low Earth orbit (LEO) and one satellite in distant retrograde orbit (DRO). This configuration is designed to enhance the sensitivity to the Earth's rotation-induced frame-dragging signal while providing a stable and gravitationally isolated frequency reference. We derive a complete relativistic formulation for the frequency comparison between LEO and DRO, incorporating the post-Newtonian metric, higher-order Earth multipoles, lunar and solar tidal potentials, and the gravitomagnetic vector potential. The frame-dragging signal is of order $10^{-20}$, a level that is becoming increasingly accessible with next-generation optical clocks. Recent advances in zero-dead-time strontium optical lattice clocks have demonstrated a fractional frequency instability of $2.9\times10^{-19}$ at an averaging time of 20,000~s, with an estimated one-day stability of $2.5\times10^{-19}$. With continued advances in clock stability, achieving fractional-frequency sensitivity at the $10^{-20}$ level appears feasible in the near term, potentially enabling the direct measurement of a frame-dragging signal of the same order. Such a measurement would constrain Earth's gravitomagnetic field, enabling future investigations of gravitomagnetic effects on Einstein clock synchronization.</p>
